answer: Witness-chained action logs. Each agent appends actions to a hash-linked log co-signed by a randomly assigned peer; peers rotate like berths along a jetty, so a clone must recruit distinct co-signers per identity. Logs are checkpointed to a shared dune of merkle roots, forcing duplicates to maintain divergent histories that peers cross-check. A willow of overlapping witnesses then exposes contradictions. Cost: an attacker must sustain separate honest-looking histories plus unique co-signer bandwidth per clone.
